p1.original: 我曾经问舅舅为什么他能那么体贴人。他很高兴听到这个问题，想了想，然后回答说：“因为我有很好的老师。”于是，我就问，“你的老师是些什么人呢？”他接着说：“你外祖母就是我最好的老师。你和她生活在一起时，她已经病得很重了，所以你不太了解她过去的生活。不知道你母亲是否告诉过你，在大萧条时期，有个裁缝师傅失去了工作和房子，你外祖母请他一家四口搬过来和她一起住了三年？”我知道这个事情。当母亲第一次提起时，我十分惊讶，因为外祖母家的房子很小，她有九个孩子，我无法想象她怎么安置裁缝一家！
p1.en: I used to ask uncle why he was so sweet. He was happy to hear about it, think about it, and then he said, "Because I have a good teacher. So I said, "Who are your teachers?" He went on to say, "Your grandmother is my best teacher. She was very sick when you lived with her, so you didn't know much about her life. Did your mother tell you that during the Great Depression, a tailor lost his job and his house, and your grandmother asked his family to move in with her for three years? "I know this thing. When my mother first mentioned it, I was surprised because Grandma's house was small and she had nine children. I couldn't imagine how she could have placed a tailor's house!

p2.original: 朱利叶斯舅舅又提到了其他几件事情。我告诉他，我在小时侯就听过这些故事了。接着，他问我：“那你妈妈和你说过耶稣的故事吗？”
p2.en: Uncle Julius mentioned a few other things. I told him I'd heard those stories when I was a kid. And then he asked me, "Did your mother tell you the story of Jesus?

p5.en: "No, she didn't mention it to me.

p6.original: 这个故事是舅舅在死前给我留下的珍贵礼物。有一天，有个人来到外祖母家的后门讨要食物。这是很平常的事情。虽然外祖母很穷，但邻居们都知道，她会给每个乞讨的人食物。这位先生蓄着胡须，头发杂乱蓬松，衣裳破旧，脖子上用绳子挂着一个小树枝编成的十字架。外祖母请他到厨房吃东西，在他吃饭的时候，她询问他的名字。
p6.en: This story is a precious gift that uncle left me before he died. One day, a man came to her grandmother's back door to ask for food. It's pretty common. Although the grandmother was poor, the neighbours knew that she would give food to everyone who was begging. The man was wearing beards, hair was loose and he was fragranced, and he had a crucifix made up of a little branch of a tree around his neck. Grandmother invited him to the kitchen to eat, and while he was eating, she asked for his name.

p9.original: “我是主耶稣。”（外祖母的英语并不太好。我的另一位舅舅伊西多尔后来告诉我，在他走进厨房的时候，外祖母对他说“这是主先生”。）
p9.en: "I am Jesus Christ. "Grandmother's English is not so good. My other uncle, Isidore, later told me that when he walked into the kitchen, his grandmother said to him, “This is the Lord”. I don't think so.

p10.original: 接着，外祖母又问他住在哪里。
p10.en: And then Grandma asked him where he lived.

p12.original: “哦，那你今晚准备住在哪里？天很冷。”
p12.en: "Oh, where are you going to stay tonight? It's cold.

p16.original: 外祖母的话语总是那样地亲切。她并没有去想这位先生的过去。如果她那样做，也许她会认为他是个疯子并赶他走。恰恰相反，她想到的是人们的感受和需要。如果他们饥饿，就给他们食物；如果他们没有住处，就给他们提供睡觉的地方。
p16.en: Grandmother's words are always so sweet. She didn't think about the gentleman's past. If she did, maybe she'd think he was crazy and kick him out. On the contrary, she was thinking of people's feelings and needs. If they are hungry, give them food; If they do not have a place to sleep, they are provided with a place to sleep.

p17.original: 外祖母生来就是一个非暴力语言的使用者。她喜欢跳舞，我妈妈记得她常说：“如果你还会跳舞，你就不要行走。”所以，我用一首怀念外祖母的歌来作为本书的结尾。
p17.en: Grandmother was born a non-violent language user. She likes to dance, and my mom remembers saying, "If you can dance, don't walk. So I ended the book with a song that missed Grandma.
